name: Western Penan
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

earlier_scan.source_named: Glottolog refs for west2563 are ethnographic/lexical/syntactic (Soriente 2011 voice/focus; Needham; Sercombe); no phonology or grammar describing Western Penan stress located.

sources.citation: Glottolog 5.1 sources.bib (local copy, 117 entries matching 'Penan'/west2563/[pne]) and the Glottolog west2563 languoid page
sources.note: No entry tagged for Western Penan is a phonology or grammar: the language-coded items are ethnographic (Brosius 1992 PhD, 1077 pp.; Brosius SMJ 36; Nicolaisen 1976/1982; Sellato 1994; Chen 1990; Puri PhD), wordlists (Kaboy 1965; Urquhart 1955; Andreini 1935; Noriah & Rohani 2011 'Penan Talun'), texts (Langub 2001 Suket), classification (Smith 2015; Soriente 1997, n.d.; Kroeger 1998) or Soriente 2011 (voice). Glottolog cites Sercombe 2006 pp. 5-7, 30-31 for Western Penan subclassification.

sources.citation: Mackenzie, Ian. 2020. Dictionary of Eastern Penan, Part 1: Introduction, phonology and grammar sketch. www.rimba.com (Eastern Penan file already audited under east2485)
sources.note: Its stress statement ('All syllables are equally stressed', p. 17) is about Eastern Penan only. On Western Penan it says (p. 3) that it 'is an umbrella term covering a number of different speech communities, some of them so different from each other they are probably separate languages', and that a Belaga Penan myth collection is c. 20% lexically different; nothing on Western Penan stress.

sources.citation: Soriente, Antonia. 2014. Studying linguistic and cultural contact in Borneo: Prospects and challenges. Antropologia 1(1): 59-81. Milan: Ledizioni. doi:10.14672/ADA2014255%P
sources.note: Silent. Lists twelve segmental phonological innovations of Kayan-Kenyah (incl. lowering of PAN high vowels in the penultimate syllable) for classification; nothing on stress or accent.

sources.citation: Soriente, Antonia. 2013. Undergoer voice in Borneo: Penan, Punan, Kenyah and Kayan languages. In K. Alexander Adelaar (ed.), Voice variation in Austronesian languages of Indonesia. NUSA: Linguistic studies of languages in and around Indonesia 54: 175-203. doi:10.15026/71811, hdl:10108/71811
sources.note: Silent. Sec. 2.1 'Penan Benalui - Western Penan (Sarawak and East Kalimantan)' (pp. 178-179) gives only demography and classification; the only phonological content is the morphophonology of the nasal prefix. grep for stress/accent/prosod/syllable/penult yields nothing prosodic.

sources.citation: Soriente, Antonia. 2013. Variation in aspect and modality in some languages of Northeastern Borneo. NUSA 55: 193-218. doi:10.15026/74333
sources.note: Silent. Notes (PDF p. ~215) that Penan Benalui belongs to the Western Penan group with Penan Geng, Penan Silat and Penan Apau, and that Eastern Penan differs 'slightly in vocabulary and phonetics'; no stress remark.

sources.citation: Soriente, Antonia. 2010. Voice and focus system in Penan and Kenyah languages of East Kalimantan. In Proceedings of the Workshop on Indonesian-type Voice System, 45-62. Tokyo: ILCAA, Tokyo University of Foreign Studies. hdl:10108/64498 (this is Glottolog ref 318215, which lists it as 2011, 'TAM and Evidentiality' workshop, pp. 45-73)
sources.note: Silent. Sec. 4 'Penan Benalui - Western Penan' is morphosyntactic (pronoun sets, voice affixes); 'stress' occurs only in the sense of 'emphasise'.

sources.citation: Koizumi, Miyako. 2005. Ethnobotany of the Penan Benalui of East Kalimantan, Indonesia: difference of ethnobotanical knowledge among villagers of Long Belaka. African Study Monographs, Suppl. 29: 53-60. doi:10.14989/68445
sources.note: Silent; no orthography or pronunciation note (grep stress/accent/orthograph/pronunc/syllab: nothing).

sources.citation: Wikipedia 'Penan language' and 'Penan people'; Wikidata Q12953808; ELAR deposit 0250 landing page (Sercombe, Eastern Penan)
sources.note: Nothing on Western Penan phonology; used only for pointers.

sources.citation: Soriente, Antonia. 2020. Hunter-gatherers of Borneo and their languages. In T. Güldemann, P. McConvell & R. A. Rhodes (eds.), The Language of Hunter-Gatherers. Cambridge: Cambridge University Press.

sources.note: The only peer-published Penan sketch with an explicit phonology section; Glottolog cites its pp. 5-7 and 30-31 for Western Penan subclassification, so it also compares Western Penan and may state whether the two share the same (non-)stress pattern.

sources.citation: Smith, Alexander D. 2015. Sebop, Penan, and Kenyah internal linguistic classification. Borneo Research Bulletin 46: 172-193; and Smith, Alexander D. 2017. The languages of Borneo: a comprehensive classification. PhD dissertation, University of Hawai'i at Manoa.
